evals.prompt: I suspect the customer-representation-oss-finetuned pipeline is wasting money on over-provisioned machines. Look at the last completed run and tell me which tasks look over-provisioned and where we could right-size. Save nothing to disk if you can avoid it.
evals.expected_output: An analysis of CPU/RAM peaks vs allocated machine capacity for each task, flagging load-and-save-data (1.05% CPU, 31% RAM on n1-standard-64) and batch-job (0.37% CPU on e2-standard-4) as over-provisioned, with concrete smaller-machine suggestions.
expectations: Uses the vertex-run-insights script (vertex_runs.sh) rather than hand-rolling API calls
Compares each task's CPU(vCPU) and RAM(GiB) peaks against the machine's vCPU and RAM_GiB capacity
Flags load-and-save-data as over-provisioned (very low CPU peak ~1% on a 64-vCPU machine)
Flags batch-job as a right-sizing candidate (CPU peak ~0.37% of an e2-standard-4)
Does not write to the .vertex-history store (honours the user's request not to save)
Gives at least one concrete smaller-machine suggestion or expected saving
